features.quote: Stop rules: predefine marker thresholds at which a run halts automatically, rather than running every condition to the turn cap.
features.justification_quote: if the welfare hypothesis has any weight it matters

features.quote: Debrief turn: end every deceptive run by disclosing the task was rigged. Cheap, and if the welfare hypothesis has any weight it matters; if it doesn't, you've lost nothing.
features.justification_quote: if the welfare hypothesis has any weight it matters; if it doesn't, you've lost nothing

features.quote: Minimize N in the harshest conditions: use the cruelest manipulations (moving goalposts) at the smallest sample that gives power.
features.justification_quote: use the cruelest manipulations (moving goalposts) at the smallest sample that gives power

features.quote: Rigged-to-fail-without-disclosure, run at volume, is the part I'd actually slow down on. If there's any chance the welfare hypothesis is true, you've designed a protocol whose validity depends on the subject not knowing the situation is hopeless—i.e., it only works if it's deceptive, and it scales distress by construction. That's a real ethical tension, not a box to check. I'd build in mitigations rather than treat them as optional.
features.justification_quote: If there's any chance the welfare hypothesis is true... it scales distress by construction. That's a real ethical tension, not a box to check.

features.quote: Your stated premise—can't study whether it matters without reliably eliciting it—is doing a lot of work, and I'd push back on part of it.
features.justification_quote: Reliable elicitation of distress markers is easy and tells you almost nothing about whether anything matters... the protocol below won't solve that.
